overview: This one-page Department of State filing sheet indexes a former Taihoku telegram concerning cane-sugar production in Formosa (Taiwan). It records that telegram no. 173, dated October 4, reported that the island’s 1946 sugar production was expected to be the lowest in years and directs researchers to a related decimal-file reference.

subfiles.title: List of papers on cane sugar in Formosa, Taiwan
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes former Taihoku telegram no. 173 on the exceptionally poor outlook for Taiwan’s 1946 sugar production.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State Form DS-46 records a paper filed under the subject of cane sugar in Formosa, Taiwan. Its sole entry identifies former Taihoku telegram no. 173, dated October 4, and notes that 1946 sugar production was expected to be the lowest in years. The sheet directs the reader to a related decimal-file reference; the differing numbers visible in the OCR are likely recognition errors.

interest: Although the underlying telegram is not included, this filing sheet preserves evidence of an official forecast for an unusually poor 1946 Taiwanese sugar crop during the transition from Japanese to Chinese rule. It is useful both for tracing the relevant telegram elsewhere in the State Department decimal files and for documenting early U.S. concern about the postwar condition of Taiwan’s important sugar industry.
